Every setting of every stage

Source: R/doc-settings-table.R
gr_settings_table.Rd

One table of every setting harnessr has, across the stages of a run: ingesting a file, cutting it into chunks, reading it, screening, extracting and writing a review, evaluating, and the session's options. vignette("settings") prints it, grouped by stage.

Usage

gr_settings_table(stage = NULL)

Arguments

stage

NULL for every stage, or one or more of "ingest", "segment", "read", "screen", "extract", "synthesise", "evaluate" and "options".

Value

A data frame with one row per setting and the columns stage, name, where (the function that takes it, as "gr_read_spec()", or "gr_options()"), default (as text: a string without quotes, the first choice of a set of choices, other values as R code), tier ("basic" for the few settings most runs change, else "advanced"), status and source (where the default came from: "measured", "cited" or "untested" and why, NA when nothing is declared), description, and guide, the guide section that explains how to choose it, as "readers#set-top-k" (the article, then the section's id), or NA.

Details

The table is built when it is asked for, from what declares each setting, so it says what the installed code does:

ingest, segment, read

The schemas of gr_ingest_spec(), gr_segment_spec() and gr_read_spec() (see gr_settings()), with their defaults, tiers and evidence. The ingest stage adds the entries of cleaner_opts and layout_opts the built-in code reads, as cleaner_opts.references_after and so on, and the read stage adds the arguments of gr_read_many().

screen, extract, synthesise, evaluate

The arguments of the functions of each stage (gr_screen(), gr_reference(), gr_calibrate(), gr_screen_sample_size() and gr_stop_test(); gr_extract(); gr_claims(), gr_outline(), gr_gaps() and gr_synthesise(); hr_benchmark(), hr_report(), hr_judge() and gr_compare()), leaving out the inputs a call works on (the documents, the client, the trace). Defaults are the functions' own, and descriptions the first sentence of each argument's help.

options

Every gr_options() option, with its default, the evidence its rule declares, and the first sentence of its entry in the help page.

Descriptions come from the installed help pages; where they cannot be read, description is NA.

See also

gr_settings() for one spec's schema, hr_sweep() to test a setting, vignette("settings")

Examples

s <- gr_settings_table()
table(s$stage)
#> 
#>   evaluate    extract     ingest    options       read     screen    segment 
#>         22          9         19         34         40         30         14 
#> synthesise 
#>         28 
s[s$tier == "basic", c("stage", "name", "default")]
